| 2022 | 4 [1] |
| 2024 | 12 [1] |

citations.quote: Synthetic net balances in units were -8 in 2021, 4 in 2022, and 12 in 2024. The year intervals are one year then two years. The records do not identify what caused the changes.
The three observations are not a forecast. A straight segment between recorded values does not establish an intermediate observation or a constant annual rate.

findings.problem: The table renders with no visible column separation, so year and balance run together: rows read as "2021-8", "20224", "202412", and the header reads as a single phrase "Year Balance (units)". Students can misread "2022 4" as the number 20224 and misread the header as one label.
findings.correction: Keep the table as a real two-column table with a clear gutter (e.g. year left-aligned, balance right-aligned with at least 40–60 px of separation, plus an optional header rule or row banding) so each year and its balance are unambiguously distinct.

findings.problem: The two side notes float in the right third with no alignment to the table, leaving a large empty band under the table and making the caveat look detached from the data it qualifies.
findings.correction: Anchor the notes to the table's top and bottom edges (or place them directly beneath the table) so the caveat reads as captioning the same three observations.

beforeFindings.problem: The rendered chart shows only the final '12 units' data label; the -8 and 4 unit values are not visible anywhere on the slide. No visible table or labeled y-axis carries them, so the negative value and the recorded series are not preserved for students.
beforeFindings.correction: Add y-axis tick labels including -8, 0, 4 and 12 units, or place visible data labels on all three points. If a table is intended, render it in an open area rather than leaving it hidden or occluded.

beforeFindings.problem: The title says the balances cross zero, but the chart has no zero baseline or labeled y-scale, so the crossing cannot be located or verified; the line only appears to rise from an unlabeled low point to 12 units.
beforeFindings.correction: Draw and label a zero line and y-axis scale so the crossing can be verified from the chart.
